exam.title: Physics 2001

parts.title: Part I – Multiple Choice Questions
parts.instructions: Part I of the paper contains 50 questions worth 1.6 points each. This file keeps only items whose stem, five options and answer were verified from the scan.

source.scan: HP Scan image PDF; Part I MCQs read from page images

exam.answer_key_note: No official key in the PDF. Answers solved independently. Skipped this batch: Q3 (option letters not reliable), Q6, Q11, Q12, Q16 (computed value not among printed options), Q24–Q28 (circuit/capacitor figures), Q33 (galvanometer exponent not reliable against the printed shunt values), Q36 (which statement is false was not reliable). Part II not included.

questions.stem: A cell membrane is 50 angstroms thick. Its thickness in meters and micrometers respectively are
explanation_steps: 1 angstrom = 10⁻¹⁰ m, so 50 angstroms = 5.0×10⁻⁹ m.
1 μm = 10⁻⁶ m, so 5.0×10⁻⁹ m = 5.0×10⁻³ μm. Answer: A.

questions.stem: The dimensions of electrical resistance are
explanation_steps: R = V/I and V = work/charge, so [R] = [energy] / ([charge][current]).
That gives M L² T⁻³ A⁻². Answer: A.

questions.stem: A machine does 3.6×10⁶ J of work in one hour. Its power in watts is
explanation_steps: Power = work/time = 3.6×10⁶ J / 3600 s = 1000 W. Answer: A.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is correct about the vectors (2i + 3j) and (i + 2j)?
explanation_steps: Two vectors are parallel only if one is a scalar multiple of the other.
2/1 ≠ 3/2, so they are not parallel. Their cross product is not zero and their dot product is 8, not zero. Answer: A.

questions.stem: A block on a spring has a kinetic energy of 3 J and the spring has an elastic potential energy of 2 J when the block is at x = 2.0 cm. The kinetic energy of the block at x = 0.0 is
explanation_steps: Mechanical energy is conserved on the spring–block system described.
At x = 0 the spring potential energy is zero, so the kinetic energy is 3 J + 2 J = 5 J. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Which one of the following equations represents motion with constant acceleration?
explanation_steps: Constant acceleration gives a position that is at most quadratic in time.
x = −5t² + 4t has a = −10 m/s². The other equations have changing acceleration or undefined motion. Answer: C.

questions.stem: The muzzle speed of a bullet from a gun is 49 m/s. The maximum horizontal distance at which the bullet can hit is
explanation_steps: Maximum range on level ground is v²/g at 45°.

questions.stem: A particle of mass 2 kg moves at 5 m/s in a uniform circular motion of radius 2 m because a cord tied to the particle is anchored at the centre. The power of the force exerted on the particle by the cord is
explanation_steps: The cord force is centripetal, so it is perpendicular to the velocity.
Power = F·v = 0. Answer: E.

questions.stem: A nuclear submarine has a horizontal hull area of 3000 m². The total weight of water on top of the submarine at a depth of 200 m is
explanation_steps: Use the printed sea-water density 1.03×10³ kg/m³ and g = 9.8 m/s².

questions.stem: 0.5 m³ of an ideal gas is heated from 300 K to 500 K at constant volume. The work done on the gas during the heating is
explanation_steps: Work done by an ideal gas is ∫P dV.
The volume is constant, so dV = 0 and the work is zero. Answer: E.

questions.stem: A thin glass plate is exactly 20 cm by 30 cm at 10°C. When its temperature is raised to 40°C, the increase in its area is (α_glass = 9×10⁻⁶ /K)
explanation_steps: Area expansion: ΔA = 2α A ΔT.

questions.stem: Which relationship between force F on a particle and its position x implies simple harmonic motion?
explanation_steps: SHM requires a restoring force proportional to displacement, F = −kx.
Only F = −6x has that form. Answer: A.

questions.stem: A car travels at 40 km/h for 2 hours, at 50 km/h for 1 hour and at 20 km/h for 0.5 hour. The average speed of the car (in km/h) is
explanation_steps: Average speed = 140/3.5 = 40 km/h. Answer: B.

questions.stem: A man walks 8 km north and then 6 km in a direction 30° north of east. His resultant displacement (in km) from his starting position is (sin 30° = 0.5, cos 30° = 0.866)
explanation_steps: East component = 6×0.866 = 5.20 km. North component = 8 + 6×0.5 = 11 km.
Resultant = √(5.20² + 11²) = √148.0 = 12.2 km, which is 12 km to the printed precision. Answer: B.

questions.stem: The length of the string of a simple pendulum is 40 cm and the mass of the bob is 0.5 kg. If g = 10 m/s², its angular frequency is
explanation_steps: The bob mass does not enter the angular frequency. Answer: A.

questions.stem: 7.72 kJ of heat raises the temperature of a 4.0 kg copper block from 300 K to 305 K. The specific heat of copper is
explanation_steps: Answer: C.

questions.stem: A coil has resistance 18 Ω at a mean temperature of 20°C and 20 Ω at 50°C. When its resistance is 21 Ω, its mean temperature (in °C) is
explanation_steps: R = R₀(1 + α ΔT). From 18 Ω to 20 Ω over 30 K, α = 2/(18×30) = 1/270 per °C.

questions.stem: Choose the INCORRECT statement.

options.A: The potential difference between two points A and B is the work done in moving a unit test charge from A to B.
options.B: The work done in carrying a finite charge between two points at the same potential is zero.
options.C: For a uniform field the relation between potential difference V_AB, field E and separation d is V_AB = Ed.
options.D: The work done is stored as electric potential energy of the charge.
options.E: The unit of potential difference is the volt, defined as V = J·s/A.

explanation_steps: 1 volt = 1 joule per coulomb = 1 J/(A·s), not J·s/A.
A–D match the standard definitions for electrostatic potential. The incorrect statement is E.

questions.stem: A cosmic-ray proton reaches the Earth near the equator with a vertical speed of 2.8×10⁷ m/s. The horizontal component of the Earth's magnetic field there is 30 μT. The ratio of the magnetic force on the proton to its weight is (m_p = 1.67×10⁻²⁷ kg, q = 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ C)
explanation_steps: The velocity is perpendicular to the horizontal field, so F_m = qvB.

questions.stem: Two parallel wires in a lamp cord are 2 mm apart. The magnitude of the force per metre between them when each carries 10 A is
explanation_steps: That is 0.01 N/m. Answer: A.

questions.stem: Choose the INCORRECT statement about the magnetic field due to a long straight current-carrying wire.

options.A: Its magnitude is proportional to the current.
options.B: Its magnitude decreases as the distance from the wire increases.
options.C: It is uniform around the wire.
options.D: Its direction is given by the right-hand rule.

explanation_steps: B = μ₀ I /(2π r) is not uniform: it changes with distance and its direction circles the wire.
A, B, D and E are correct. The incorrect statement is C.

questions.stem: A closed conducting loop is moved in a uniform magnetic field. The induced emf in the loop

options.A: depends only on the resistance of the loop.
options.B: depends on the shape of the loop.
options.C: depends on the magnitude of the magnetic field.
options.E: depends on the rate at which the loop is moved.

explanation_steps: Translating a closed loop in a uniform field does not change the flux through it.
The induced emf is therefore zero. Answer: D.

questions.stem: Choose the INCORRECT statement.

options.A: If the magnetic field through a circuit changes with time, an emf is induced in the circuit.
options.B: Lenz's law states that the direction of the induced emf is always opposite to that of the magnetic field which induced it.
options.C: For a given rate of change of flux, a coil of many turns has a larger induced emf than a single turn.
options.D: If two circuits are close but not touching, a change of current in one can induce an emf in the other.
options.E: An isolated circuit carrying a varying current induces a back emf in itself that opposes the change in current.

explanation_steps: Lenz's law says the induced emf opposes the change in flux, not that it is always opposite the inducing field.
A, C, D and E are consistent with Faraday's law and self-induction. The incorrect statement is B.

questions.stem: The primary winding of a transformer has 200 turns and the secondary has 50 turns. If the current in the secondary is 40 A, the current in the primary is
explanation_steps: For an ideal transformer, I_p / I_s = N_s / N_p.

questions.stem: The power factor in an a.c. circuit in which X_L = X_C
explanation_steps: When X_L = X_C the circuit is resonant and the phase angle is zero.
The power factor cos φ is 1. Answer: B.

questions.stem: A wave of amplitude A interferes with another wave of the same kind whose frequency is different but whose amplitude is also A. The resulting wave has an amplitude
explanation_steps: Two equal-amplitude waves of different frequency produce beats.
The resultant amplitude varies between 0 and 2A. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Waves of length 5 m pass an anchored boat 1.25 s apart. The speed of the waves is

options.E: Impossible to tell from the information given.

explanation_steps: The time between successive crests is the period, T = 1.25 s.
v = λ/T = 5/1.25 = 4 m/s. Answer: A.

questions.stem: A force of 50 N is applied to the input piston of a hydraulic system. The input area is 60 cm² and the output area is 15 cm². The force the output piston exerts is
explanation_steps: Pressure is transmitted, so F_out / F_in = A_out / A_in.
F_out = 50 × 15/60 = 12.5 N. Answer: E.

questions.stem: A horizontal pipe of 10 cm² cross-section joins a pipe of 50 cm². The speed in the smaller pipe is 6 m/s and the pressure there is 200 kPa. The speed and pressure in the larger pipe are
explanation_steps: Continuity: A₁v₁ = A₂v₂ gives v₂ = 6 × 10/50 = 1.2 m/s.
Bernoulli: P₂ = 200 kPa + ½ρ(v₁² − v₂²) = 200 + 0.5×1000×(36 − 1.44)/1000 kPa = 217.3 kPa. Answer: B.

questions.stem: The following forces act on an object: 10 N north, 20 N southeast and 5 N west. The magnitude of their resultant is (sin 45° = cos 45° = 0.707)
explanation_steps: Take east and north as positive. Southeast contributes 14.14 N east and −14.14 N north.
Resultant = √(9.14² + 4.14²) = 10.0 N. Answer: E.

questions.stem: A cannon fires a shell at 1.7 km/s at 55° to the horizontal. The range and time of flight are (sin 55° = 0.819, cos 55° = 0.574, g = 9.8 m/s²)
explanation_steps: Time of flight = 2 v sin 55° / g = 2×1700×0.819/9.8 = 284 s. Answer: D.

questions.stem: A skater has moment of inertia 3.0 kg·m² with arms outstretched and 1.0 kg·m² with arms at her sides. She spins at 1.0 rev/s with arms out, then pulls her arms in. Her final angular speed and the work she has done are
explanation_steps: Angular momentum is conserved, so ω_f = 3.0 × 1.0 = 3.0 rev/s.
Work done = ΔKE = 118 J. Answer: D.

questions.stem: Choose the INCORRECT answer. When an atom decays by emission of a β particle

options.A: the mass number of the daughter nucleus remains the same.
options.B: the mass of the daughter nucleus is approximately equal to that of the parent nucleus.
options.C: the atomic number of the daughter nucleus decreases by 1.
options.D: the daughter nucleus occupies a different position in the periodic table.
options.E: charge is conserved in a β decay.

explanation_steps: β⁻ emission raises the atomic number by 1; it does not decrease it.
Mass number is unchanged, charge is conserved, and the daughter is a different element. The incorrect statement is C.
